raw_response:
Aiya, let me think about this year's planting...

I'm 46 now, been working this little 5 mu piece since I was twenty. My wife helps in the fields, our older boy sometimes goes to town for construction work when there's nothing to do here, and the younger one is still in school. So most days it's just me and the wife out there. 5 mu is not a lot — you can't get rich from it, but with the kidneybean and the maize together, we manage.

I usually put about 3 mu to maize and the other 2 mu to kidneybean. Maize we need for ourselves and to sell some, plus the stalks for the neighbor's cows (he gives us a little money or helps us with his tractor). Kidneybean sells for a decent price when the traders come around — last year Old Wang from the next village got almost 8 yuan per jin for his, though mine didn't look as nice so I got less. That's why I keep growing it though — one good kidneybean year pays for a lot.

For the maize, I plant in late April, after the ground warms up. Can't be too early or the seed rots. I buy the hybrid seed from the shop in town — one of those Zhengdan types, same as most people around here use. Costs maybe 50-60 yuan for enough for my 3 mu. I don't save maize seed, everyone says hybrid seed from saved grain doesn't grow right.

Before planting I put down a bag of compound fertilizer — the 15-15-15 one — about one bag per mu, maybe a little less because bags are expensive this year. Then when the maize is about knee-high, I topdress with urea, maybe half a bag per mu. That's what my father did and what most people do. If the leaves look yellow I'll add a bit more, if they look dark green I save the fertilizer. I don't measure exactly, you learn by looking.

Water — the well is there but the electricity costs real money. I irrigate when I plant if it's dry, and once more if July is really hot with no rain. Two times usually, sometimes three if it's a drought year like 2022 was. I flood the furrows, not sprinkler, we don't have that kind of equipment.

Pests — I spray herbicide once after planting, otherwise the weeds eat everything and my back can't take hoeing 3 mu anymore. If I see borers in the stalk I'll spray once, but usually it's not too bad.

For the kidneybean, I plant in May, a bit later than the maize. I save some seed from my best plants last year, that way I don't have to buy as much. Kidneybean doesn't need much fertilizer — my father always said beans make their own fertilizer somehow — so I just put down a little compound fertilizer before planting, maybe half a bag per mu, no topdress. I irrigate once or twice. The kidneybean needs more careful picking work when it's ready, that's where me and the wife both really have to be in the field, sometimes the older boy stays home from town to help for a week.

Total I spend maybe 2000 yuan or a bit more on everything. If I had more cash I'd put more fertilizer on the maize — Old Liu down the row puts way more and gets better yield — but I'd rather keep a few hundred yuan in hand in case someone gets sick or something breaks.
